title: A CTE read twice in one statement is evaluated once
verdict: materialized once by default; NOT MATERIALIZED evaluates it per reference
description: A CTE that a statement reads twice is evaluated once by default: a CTE with random() joined with itself on its key has no row whose two reads differ, in three runs; a scalar CTE read by two subqueries gives equal values. WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED does the same; WITH ... AS NOT MATERIALIZED evaluates the CTE per reference, and every row's two reads differ.

So a check root and a sink root written as one statement over one CTE read the same evaluation of a double SUM in it on DuckDB, unless the CTE is NOT MATERIALIZED. The statement runs in one transaction's snapshot (MVCC), so both reads see one version of the tables.
reference: The reference evaluates a plan once per catalog: Rel.eval of a shared subplan is one value. Which evaluation an engine reads is outside the model (#929's margin check).

evidence.sql: CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT range AS i FROM range(1000); WITH c AS (SELECT i, random() AS r FROM t) SELECT count(*) FROM c a JOIN c b USING (i) WHERE a.r <> b.r
evidence.observed: 0 (three runs); with WITH c AS NOT MATERIALIZED: 1000; WITH c AS MATERIALIZED: 0; (SELECT r FROM c) = (SELECT r FROM c) for a scalar CTE: true
